title: Diagnostic: Swift 6 Catches a Data Race
hints: Swift 6 rejects sharing a non-`Sendable` class between concurrent tasks.
Make `Counter` a plain class and mutate one instance both inside a `Task` and in the enclosing function.
jsBridge: Swift 6 **compile-time data-race safety**: sharing a non-`Sendable` mutable class across tasks is a compile error. JS never needs this (single thread), and most languages only find races at runtime (TSan).

compass.q: JS is race-free by being single-threaded. Swift 6 is race-free by construction with multiple threads. What's the price (annotations, `Sendable`)?
Fixes: make it an `actor`, make it `final class: Sendable` with immutable state, or `@MainActor`. When is each right?
`@unchecked Sendable`: when is it legitimate, and why is it an escape hatch?
Migrating an app to Swift 6 mode: which warnings dominate, and what's the strategy?
